title: Nasruddin Tale 178: The Lost Diamond in the Dust
summary: A traveler dropped a glittering diamond into the muddy street. Passersby searched frantically, pushing each other into the dirt....
full_text:
Mulla Nasruddin was famous throughout the province for his uncanny ability to confound pompous scholars, corrupt magistrates, and nosy neighbors with his razor-sharp eccentric wit. On this particular morning, A traveler dropped a glittering diamond into the muddy street. Passersby searched frantically, pushing each other into the dirt..... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that a diamond trampled in dust is still a gem; mud upon a prince does not taint his soul.
moral: A diamond trampled in dust is still a gem; mud upon a prince does not taint his soul.
